newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PBGC had $869 million surplus in fiscal 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PBGC had $869 million surplus in fiscal 1996.

text.p: The White House announced on Monday that the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corp. (PBGC) had a surplus of $869 million last year, the first in the federal agency's 22-year history.

The PBGC, which insures pensions for more than 42 million U.S. workers, had assets of $12.04 billion and liabilities of $11.17 billion in fiscal 1996, which ended September 30, 1996, the White House said in a statement.

It also unveiled the following measures: resubmitting legislation to tighten up pension plan audits; creating a toll-free telephone hotline to give workers information on pension protections; and rules to force companies to invest worker pension contributions more quickly.

The legislation would close a loophole permitting $950 billion in pension plan assets to escape meaningful audits, require prompt reporting if criminal acts are discovered and ensure that only qualified professionals conduct audits.
A White House official said the legislation was submitted to Congress last year but did not make it to a vote.
The White House also unveiled a toll-free number, 1 800 998 7542, for workers to get publications on protecting their pensions.

It also said that federal rules went into effect last month requiring employers to deposit worker contributions into pension plans no later than 15 business days after the end of the month when the contribution was made.
The White House said it estimated that this change would increase earnings for participants and beneficiaries by a total of nearly $700 million over the next 10 years.
President Clinton was scheduled to announce the various pension initiatives at 1330 EST (1830 GMT) on Monday.
